risk: Vehicles are acquired outside the approved capital plan, or disposed of below market value to related parties.
audit_objective: Confirm fleet additions and disposals are authorised, competitively sourced, and disposal proceeds are complete and at arm's length.
what_to_review: Capital plan approval and variance to actual additions
Tender or quotation file for each acquisition above threshold
Disposal method used — auction, trade-in, private sale
Residual value assumptions versus realised proceeds
procedures: Reconcile the fixed asset register to the fleet management system and vehicle licensing records; investigate units in one and not the other.
Select a sample of additions and trace to capital plan approval, business case and competitive quotes.
For all disposals in the period, recompute gain/loss and agree proceeds to bank receipt.
Match buyer names and addresses against the employee and vendor master for related-party indicators.
Compare realised proceeds against an independent used-vehicle price guide for a sample of units.
red_flags: Disposals clustered just below the approval threshold
Repeat buyers across multiple disposals
Units written down shortly before sale
Assets still insured or licensed after recorded disposal
plain: Vehicles are valuable and easy to sell cheaply to the wrong person if nobody is watching the disposal.

risk: Fuel is drawn for personal vehicles or resold, and the loss is buried in normal consumption variance.
audit_objective: Determine whether fuel consumption is complete, authorised, and reconciled to vehicle activity at the unit level.
what_to_review: Fuel card issuance and cancellation process
Consumption per kilometre by unit against the fleet norm
Transactions outside route, hours, or tank capacity
Reconciliation of bulk fuel site dips to dispensed volumes
procedures: Obtain the full fuel card transaction file and join it to telematics GPS data; test for fills where the vehicle was more than 5 km from the station.
Test for fill volumes exceeding the unit's tank capacity, and for two fills of the same card within a short window.
Rank units by litres per 100 km and investigate the outlier tail with the terminal manager.
Confirm cards for terminated drivers were cancelled within the policy window.
For bulk sites, reconcile deliveries plus opening dip less closing dip to dispensed volumes; investigate unexplained shrinkage.
red_flags: Fills on non-operating days or outside shift hours
Odometer readings entered as round numbers or unchanged
Consumption spikes confined to one terminal
Manual PIN overrides at the pump
evidence: Bulk fuel delivery notes and dip records
plain: Fuel is easy to take and hard to trace, which makes it one of the most common losses in any fleet business.

risk: Preventive maintenance is deferred to protect operating margin, exposing the company to breakdowns, accidents and regulatory sanction.
audit_objective: Assess whether the maintenance programme is executed on schedule and whether defects reported by drivers are actually closed.
what_to_review: Preventive maintenance schedule compliance by unit
Driver vehicle inspection reports and defect close-out
Out-of-service orders and roadside inspection results
Third-party repair vendor rates versus contract
procedures: Extract the PM schedule and compute on-time completion by terminal; test whether overdue units continued in revenue service.
Trace a sample of driver-reported defects through to a work order and confirmed repair, measuring days open.
Obtain regulator roadside inspection data and reconcile out-of-service findings to internal maintenance records.
Recompute a sample of third-party repair invoices against contracted labour rates and parts mark-up.
red_flags: Defects repeatedly re-reported on the same unit
PM completions recorded in bulk at period end
High share of repairs at a single vendor
Inspection sign-offs by staff not on shift
plain: Skipping maintenance saves money this month and causes breakdowns, accidents and regulator action later.

risk: Shipments are delivered but never invoiced, or are invoiced at the wrong rate, weight or accessorial — revenue leakage that never appears in a variance.
audit_objective: Verify that every delivered shipment is billed, once, at the contracted rate, with all applicable accessorial charges captured.
what_to_review: Accessorial charge capture — waiting time, residential, re-delivery, fuel surcharge
procedures: Reconcile delivered shipments in the operations system to invoiced shipments in billing; quantify and age the unbilled population.
Re-price a sample of invoices independently from the contract rate table and quantify the variance.
Analyse manual rate overrides by user; test the largest for approval evidence.
Test dimensional re-weigh exceptions to confirm the corrected charge was billed.
Analyse credit notes by reason code, customer and issuer for concentration.
red_flags: Unbilled shipments ageing beyond the billing window
Overrides concentrated in one user or customer
Accessorial capture rate far below peer terminals
Credits issued shortly after month end
kpis: Revenue leakage as % of billed revenue
plain: Delivering a shipment and never invoicing it is pure lost revenue, and it does not show up as a variance anywhere.

risk: Discounts and fuel surcharge caps are granted outside delegated authority, eroding margin on long-term contracts.
audit_objective: Confirm customer pricing reflects properly authorised terms and that contract profitability is monitored after signature.
procedures: Select the largest contracts by revenue and agree discount levels to the delegation of authority matrix.
Recompute the fuel surcharge applied against the contractual index for a sample of months.
Compare contracted volume commitments to actual shipped volumes and test whether shortfall charges were billed.
Review post-award profitability reporting and test whether loss-making contracts are escalated.
red_flags: Discounts approved by the salesperson's direct report only
Surcharge caps not reflected in the rate engine
Contracts auto-renewing without repricing
Margin below cost-to-serve with no escalation
plain: Discounts agreed by salespeople outside their authority quietly erode the margin on multi-year contracts.

risk: Purchased transportation is bought at spot rates when contracted capacity was available, inflating cost per shipment.
audit_objective: Evaluate whether linehaul capacity decisions follow the planning process and whether purchased transportation is procured at the best available rate.
procedures: Analyse trailer cube and weight utilisation by lane; identify structurally under-loaded lanes.
Compare spot purchases to available contracted capacity on the same lane and date; quantify the premium paid.
Recompute a sample of carrier invoices against the rate confirmation, including accessorials and detention.
Test the approval trail for spot buys above the contracted rate.
red_flags: Spot buys concentrated with one broker
Repeated detention charges at the same terminal
Utilisation reported without reconciliation to scale data
Rate confirmations issued after the move
plain: Buying transport at short notice costs far more than using capacity already under contract.

risk: Cargo is lost, damaged or stolen in the terminal and the loss is absorbed as an operating expense without root-cause investigation.
audit_objective: Assess the integrity of custody controls over freight in the terminal and the completeness of loss reporting.
what_to_review: Physical security — access control, CCTV coverage, seal integrity
Claims recovery from carriers and insurers
procedures: Walk the terminal and observe scanning discipline at induction, sort and load; compare observed practice to the procedure.
Extract shipments with a missing scan event and test whether each was investigated.
Test seal number recording against trailer manifests for inbound and outbound loads.
Reconcile the OS&D log to claims paid and to the general ledger loss account.
Review terminal access lists against active employee records.
red_flags: Losses clustered by shift, lane or employee
Seal numbers recorded as sequential or blank
CCTV coverage gaps at high-value cages
Claims written off below the investigation threshold
evidence: Access control logs and CCTV retention records
plain: Freight changes hands repeatedly in a terminal, and each handover is an opportunity for it to go missing.

risk: Drivers operate beyond legal hours-of-service limits or with lapsed licences and medical certification, creating liability and regulatory exposure.
audit_objective: Determine whether driver qualification files are complete and hours-of-service limits are monitored and enforced.
what_to_review: Licence and medical certificate expiry monitoring
Electronic logging device data and edits
Use of owner-operators and their compliance status
procedures: Sample driver files and test for licence, abstract, medical certificate, training records and annual review.
Extract ELD data and quantify violations by driver and terminal; test disciplinary follow-up for the most frequent offenders.
Analyse ELD log edits by user — edits made by dispatch rather than the driver warrant challenge.
Cross-check active drivers against the licence expiry report on the audit date.
red_flags: Log edits concentrated near the violation threshold
Unassigned driving time
Drivers dispatched with expired medicals
Owner-operators outside the compliance monitoring scope
plain: Drivers over their legal hours or without valid licences create liability the company cannot insure away.

risk: Dangerous goods are accepted, or cross-border shipments are declared, without the required documentation and classification, exposing the company to penalties and shipment seizure.
audit_objective: Confirm regulated shipments are correctly classified, documented and handled by trained personnel.
what_to_review: Training and certification currency for handlers
Customs declaration accuracy and tariff classification
procedures: Sample dangerous goods shipments and test declaration, placarding, packaging and handler certification.
Re-perform tariff classification on a sample of cross-border shipments and quantify duty variance.
Test that denied-party screening runs on every consignee and that hits are cleared by compliance, not operations.
Review regulator correspondence, penalties and corrective action closure.
red_flags: Screening exceptions cleared by the booking agent
Classification changed after a duty query
Training certificates expiring without replacement
Recurring penalties for the same defect
plain: Dangerous goods and customs errors stop shipments and bring penalties, sometimes personal ones.

risk: Subcontracted carriers are engaged without insurance, safety rating or contract, transferring their liability back to the company.
audit_objective: Verify that every carrier moving freight has been qualified, contracted and monitored throughout the engagement.
what_to_review: Payment to carriers not in the approved master
procedures: Reconcile carriers paid in the period to the approved carrier master; investigate every payee not on the master.
Test insurance certificate expiry against the dates freight was actually tendered to each carrier.
Re-check current safety ratings for the top carriers by spend and test escalation of downgrades.
Review contracts for indemnity, sub-contracting prohibition and audit rights.
red_flags: Carriers paid with no contract on file
Insurance lapses covered by an expired certificate on file
Freight tendered to carriers with conditional safety ratings
Single-source lanes without competitive review
plain: When another carrier moves your freight, their insurance and safety record become your problem.

risk: Payments are made to fictitious vendors, or to genuine vendors at bank details altered by a fraudster.
audit_objective: Determine whether vendor master changes are independently verified and whether the payment population contains indicators of fraud or duplication.
what_to_review: Vendor creation and bank change verification
Segregation between vendor maintenance, invoice entry and payment release
procedures: Match the vendor master against the employee master on bank account, address, tax ID and phone number.
Test all bank detail changes in the period for evidence of independent call-back verification to a number obtained from an independent source.
Run duplicate payment analytics on invoice number, amount, date and vendor across near-matches.
Identify vendors reactivated after long dormancy and test the first payment after reactivation.
Test system access to confirm no user can both maintain the vendor and release the payment.
red_flags: Bank change immediately followed by a large payment
Vendors sharing a bank account
Invoices just below the approval threshold
Vendor address matching an employee address
plain: Payments to suppliers are the most common route for money to leave a company fraudulently.

risk: Users retain access after role change or termination, or hold combinations of access that allow a transaction to be initiated and approved by the same person.
audit_objective: Assess whether logical access is granted, reviewed and removed in line with role requirements and segregation of duties rules.
what_to_review: Access to production data and direct database changes
procedures: Reconcile active system accounts to the active employee list; test every orphan account.
Measure elapsed days from termination to access removal across all leavers in the period.
Run the SoD conflict matrix against current role assignments and quantify unmitigated conflicts.
Test whether the last recertification was completed by the business owner and whether flagged removals actually occurred.
Review privileged account activity logs for direct data changes outside change management.
red_flags: Recertification approved in bulk on a single day
Generic accounts shared by a team
Firefighter access left permanently enabled
Removals flagged but never executed
plain: People who change jobs or leave often keep their old system access, which is how small problems become large ones.

risk: Concerns raised through the ethics line are not investigated independently, or undisclosed conflicts of interest influence supplier selection.
audit_objective: Evaluate whether the ethics reporting channel is trusted and effective, and whether conflicts of interest are disclosed and managed.
what_to_review: Ethics line availability, anonymity and awareness
Case triage, investigation independence and closure
procedures: Review the case log for volume, category, ageing and closure quality; test a sample end to end.
Test whether cases implicating management were investigated by someone outside that reporting line.
Reconcile conflict of interest declarations to the employee population and test completeness for decision-makers.
Match declared interests against the vendor master and investigate transactions with connected parties.
red_flags: Very low case volume relative to headcount
Cases closed as unsubstantiated with no documented work
Declarations missing from procurement and finance staff
Reporters subsequently exiting the business
plain: If people do not trust the confidential reporting line, management is the last to know about problems.
